# Review: Aeration Blower Control Narrative (WWTP Upgrade)

**Recommendation: Do not release to the contractor yet.** The draft has two internal contradictions (items 2 and 5), one process-unsafe failure response (item 3), and one equipment- and personnel-unsafe restart rule (item 6). It also has no states, sequences, surge protection, alarm list or test methods. A contractor cannot build or FAT-test from it as written.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Item 2 | **Contradiction.** The header setpoint is called "fixed at 7.5 psig", but the next sentence has most-open-valve (MOV) logic resetting it. Both cannot be true. | Define PIC-920 setpoint as remote-set by MOV logic, clamped between a minimum and maximum in the setpoint list (SP-04/05). Define 7.5 psig as the fallback or initial value only (SP-03). |
| R-02 | Items 2 and 5 | **Unit and value conflict.** Item 2 uses psig, item 5 uses inH2O. 160/165 inH2O is about 5.8/6.0 psig, which is well below the 7.5 psig setpoint. At the stated setpoint the stage-on condition can never occur. | Use one unit for PIT-920 throughout (recommend psig or inH2O to match the instrument range). Move all values to the setpoint list. |
| R-03 | Item 5 | **Staging on header pressure conflicts with MOV reset.** MOV logic moves the pressure setpoint on purpose, so pressure is not a reliable signal of blower capacity. | Stage on blower capacity instead. Stage on when running blowers are at maximum output (IGV position or flow) and PIC-920 is below setpoint for the stage-on delay. Stage off when blowers are at minimum turndown for the stage-off delay. |
| R-04 | Item 5 | Stage-off has no time delay, and the 5 inH2O deadband is narrow. Expect short-cycling, excess motor starts, and surge events at stage changes. | Add a stage-off delay, a minimum run time, a minimum off time, and maximum starts per hour (SP-10 to SP-14). Add a lead/lag/standby selection and rotation rule. |
| R-05 | Item 3 | **Unsafe failure response.** Closing the air valve on bad DO starves the basin. Results: anoxic/septic conditions, solids settling in the basin, and permit risk. If several valves close, the blowers can deadhead and surge. Under-aeration costs more than over-aeration here. | On bad AIT-90x: set AIC-90x to manual, hold the last good output (or go to the fallback position in SP-07), and alarm. Exclude the valve from MOV selection while its DO is bad. |
| R-06 | Item 6 | **Unsafe restart.** Simultaneous auto-restart of all blowers causes inrush (critical on standby generator), restart of rotating blowers before coast-down, and surge risk. There is no warning to personnel. | Restore power to a "Stopped – restart pending" state. Restart blowers one at a time through the normal start sequence and permissives, after a coast-down and settle delay, with a stagger delay. Make this an operator-selectable option (auto restart enable). Confirm with operations and the electrical engineer for generator loading. |
| R-07 | Item 7 | Not a requirement. No tag, no value, no delay, no latch/reset, and no trip action (motor stop, IGV close, blow-off open). | Write as a C&E row (see below). Get the trip value from the blower vendor. |
| R-08 | Item 7 | Other blower protections are missing: surge, high bearing temperature, high motor winding temperature, high discharge temperature, low lube oil pressure (if oil-lubricated), and motor overload. | Add C&E rows. Define which protections are in the vendor control panel and which are in the PLC. |
| R-09 | Item 4 | The discharge valve has no tag. It is not clear whether "discharge valve" means the isolation valve or the blow-off valve. Many multistage centrifugal vendors need blow-off open at start. Other permissives are missing: no active trip, MCC ready, blower in Remote, lube oil OK. | Tag every permissive. Confirm the start valve line-up with the blower vendor. Write the start as a sequence table (below). |
| R-10 | Item 2 | The PIC-920 output is not defined: IGV position, VFD speed, or both. Load sharing between running blowers is not defined. | State the final element (for example ZC-931 to 933 for IGVs). State equal-output load sharing among blowers in Auto. |
| R-11 | Items 1–2 | No surge protection or minimum flow is defined. With MOV logic lowering pressure and valves at minimum, a blower can operate left of the surge line. | Add a blow-off valve control or vendor surge controller interface. Add a surge alarm and trip. |
| R-12 | Item 1 | No minimum valve position. Fine-bubble basins need minimum air for mixing and diffuser protection. No maximum air limit. | Add a minimum (SP-08) and maximum output clamp on FCV-911 to 914. |
| R-13 | Item 2 | MOV logic does not define its inputs (exclude valves in Manual, out of service, or with bad DO), its deadband, its rate of change, or what happens if all valves are excluded. | Add these rules (FR-AER-012 to 015 below). |
| R-14 | Whole document | No ISA-106 states or modes. No Hand/Off/Auto, Local/Remote, or operator interface definition. | Add a state table for each blower and the aeration system (below). Get operations sign-off. |
| R-15 | Whole document | Abnormal handling is incomplete: bad PIT-920, bad valve position feedback, comms loss to the vendor panel/MCC, PLC restart, and fail positions of FCV-911 to 914 and IGVs. | Add an abnormal handling section (below). |
| R-16 | Item 1 | No DO probe maintenance mode. Probe cleaning or calibration produces bad readings that drive the valve. | Add a "probe maintenance" hold that freezes AIC-90x output and suppresses its alarms. |
| R-17 | Items 1, 2, 5 | Numbers in prose (2.0 mg/L, 7.5 psig, 85%, 160/165 inH2O, 2 min). | Move to the setpoint list. Reference by ID. |
| R-18 | Whole document | No requirement IDs and no test methods. | Assign FR-AER-NNN and a FAT/SAT method to each. |
| R-19 | Whole document | No interlock chart, alarm list, or SIS reference. | Add C&E rows and the alarm list below. State "No SIF in this module" if the HAZOP/LOPA confirms it. |
| R-20 | Items 2, 7 | STE: item 7 is a fragment. "Most-open-valve logic" is undefined. "Maintain", "hold", and "adjust" are used for the same idea. | Define MOV once. Use one verb per meaning ("control to"). Rewrite as imperative or declarative sentences of 25 words max. |
| R-21 | Whole document | No open items, owners, or dates. No revision block or change log. | Add both. The narrative goes under MOC after construction starts. |

## Provisional setpoint list

Values marked "confirm" are my proposals. The consultant must confirm or replace them with the process design and vendor data.

| ID | Parameter | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | DO setpoint, AIC-901 to 904 | 2.0 | mg/L | From draft |
| SP-02 | MOV target position | 85 | % open | From draft |
| SP-03 | PIC-920 initial / fallback setpoint | 7.5 | psig | From draft (confirm as max) |
| SP-04 | PIC-920 setpoint minimum | 6.0 | psig | Confirm (diffuser submergence + losses) |
| SP-05 | PIC-920 setpoint maximum | 7.5 | psig | Confirm |
| SP-06 | MOV reset rate limit / deadband | 0.1 psi/min / ±5 % | — | Confirm |
| SP-07 | FCV fallback position on bad DO | Last good output | % | Confirm |
| SP-08 | FCV minimum position (mixing) | 20 | % open | Confirm with diffuser vendor |
| SP-09 | Stage-on delay | 2 | min | From draft |
| SP-10 | Stage-on capacity threshold (IGV) | 95 | % | Confirm |
| SP-11 | Stage-off turndown threshold (IGV) / delay | 10 % / 5 min | — | Confirm |
| SP-12 | Minimum run time / minimum off time | 30 / 15 | min | Confirm with motor vendor |
| SP-13 | Maximum starts per hour per blower | 3 | starts/h | Confirm with motor vendor |
| SP-14 | Power restore settle delay / restart stagger | 60 / 120 | s | Confirm with electrical |
| SP-15 | Blower coast-down lockout after stop | 5 | min | Confirm with blower vendor |
| SP-16 | Start sequence step timeout | 30 | s | Confirm |
| SP-17 | High vibration alarm / trip / delay | TBD | in/s / s | Blower vendor |
| SP-18 | Low header pressure alarm | SP-04 minus 0.5 | psig | Confirm |
| SP-19 | Low / high DO alarm | 0.5 / 4.0 | mg/L | Confirm |

## Proposed state table (each blower B-1/2/3)

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Out of Service | Blower stopped | Stopped | Operator | Manual |
| Stopped | No active trip; coast-down lockout (SP-15) complete | Starting, Out of Service | Operator or staging logic | Automatic in Auto; manual in Manual |
| Starting | Start permissives met (C&E row P-1) | Running, Tripped, Stopping | Sequence | Automatic |
| Running | Start sequence complete | Stopping, Tripped | — | Automatic |
| Stopping | — | Stopped, Tripped | Operator or staging logic | Automatic |
| Tripped | Any trip cause | Stopped (after reset) | Interlock | Operator reset required |
| Restart Pending | Power restored, blower was running, auto restart enabled | Starting, Stopped | Power restore logic | Automatic after SP-14 delays |

## Proposed start sequence (each blower)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify permissives (P-1) | All permissives true | SP-16 | Abort to Stopped. Alarm "Start failed – permissive". |
| 2 | Open blow-off valve, close IGV | Blow-off open and ZSC-93x closed | SP-16 | Abort to Stopped. Alarm. |
| 3 | Start motor | Motor run feedback true | SP-16 | Stop motor. Go to Tripped. Alarm "Fail to start". |
| 4 | Open discharge valve | ZSO discharge open | SP-16 | Stop motor. Go to Tripped. |
| 5 | Close blow-off, release IGV to PIC-920 | Blow-off closed | SP-16 | Stop motor. Go to Tripped. |

## Proposed C&E rows (pending chart)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| High vibration (SP-17) | Stop B-x, close IGV, open blow-off | Latched | Operator reset at HMI after cause clears |
| Surge detected | Open blow-off; trip B-x on repeat | Latched | Operator reset at HMI |
| High bearing / winding / discharge temperature | Stop B-x | Latched | Local reset at vendor panel, then HMI |
| Low lube oil pressure (if applicable) | Stop B-x | Latched | Local reset |
| Motor overload / MCC fault | Stop B-x | Latched | Reset at MCC |
| P-1: permissives not met | Block start of B-x | Auto-reset | Clears when permissives true |

## Proposed alarm list (pending alarm database)

| Alarm | Response |
|---|---|
| AIT-90x bad PV | Check probe. AIC-90x holds output. Use probe maintenance mode for cleaning. |
| AIT-90x low / high DO (SP-19) | Check FCV-91x position and header pressure. |
| PIT-920 bad PV | Check transmitter. Blowers hold last output. MOV reset stops. |
| PIT-920 low header pressure (SP-18) | Check for standby blower start failure or a pipe leak. |
| B-x trip (each cause) | Find the cause. Reset after correction. |
| B-x fail to start | Check permissives and MCC. |
| Comms loss to vendor panel / MCC | Check network. See abnormal handling. |
| All FCVs excluded from MOV | Header setpoint goes to SP-03. Check DO probes and valve modes. |

## Proposed abnormal handling requirements (STE-edited)

- **FR-AER-020** If AIT-90x has a bad PV, AIC-90x goes to Manual and holds the last good output (SP-07). FCV-91x does not close. *Test: force bad quality at FAT.*
- **FR-AER-021** If PIT-920 has a bad PV, the running blowers hold their last output. The MOV reset stops. *Test: force bad quality.*
- **FR-AER-022** If position feedback on FCV-91x is bad, the MOV logic excludes FCV-91x. *Test: force bad quality.*
- **FR-AER-023** If the PLC loses comms with a blower panel, the blower continues at its last output. The PLC does not start or stop that blower. *Test: disconnect the network at FAT.*
- **FR-AER-024** On loss of instrument air, FCV-911 to 914 fail open (confirm). The IGVs fail to the vendor position. *Test: isolate air at SAT.*
- **FR-AER-025** After power restores, each blower that was running goes to Restart Pending. Blowers restart one at a time with the SP-14 delays, only if auto restart is enabled. *Test: simulate power loss at FAT.*

**WARNING (for the HMI and O&M manual):** Keep away from the blowers when auto restart is enabled. The blowers can start without an operator command after power restores.

Due dates are placeholders; adjust them to the project schedule. Ask the consultant to issue the revised narrative in the template structure, with FR-AER-NNN IDs and test methods. Ask them to replace these provisional lists with the formal setpoint list, C&E chart, and alarm database before release.
